Senses.Explanation: Literally, “the one phrase before sound.” Across 89 occurrences in 55 allowlisted texts, it is chiefly a public-interview question and case-commentary heading, not a term the corpus leaves outside speech. Asked “what is the phrase before sound?” one master answers with the vocalization “un” (吽), and another says, “it is just like not saying” (恰似不道). Huanglian directly answers, “before sound there is no phrase; after the sound, bring your question” (聲前無句，聲後問將來). Later addresses make contrary predicates within the same public record: one says “everyone originally has” the phrase, while the Blue Cliff Record says “the thousand sages do not transmit” it. These are attested answers and claims, not grounds for choosing an ineffable reading. Zen bends the temporal phrase into a recurrent interview prompt whose answers may themselves be spoken sounds; this entry preserves that observable deployment and the corpus’s own disagreement.
Senses.Note: The phrase as question, heading, and quoted line denotes the same interview expression. Different answers—including sound, refusal, possession, and denial—are readings or responses, not different things and therefore not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是聲前一句。師曰吽。曰轉後如何。師曰。是什麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 景德傳燈錄, Xuanquan Yan section. An unnamed monk questioning Xuanquan Yan is the exact speaker who asks for the phrase before sound; Xuanquan responds with a lowing sound. All six attribution rungs leave the monk personally unnamed; Yantou Quanhuo is not the section subject.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是聲前一句。師曰。恰似不道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 景德傳燈錄, Heyushan Guanghui section. An unnamed monk questioning Heyushan Guanghui is the exact speaker who asks for the phrase before sound; Guanghui answers, ‘it is exactly as if it were not said.’ All six attribution rungs leave the monk personally unnamed; Caoshan Benji is the lineage teacher, not the actor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問黃連和尚：如何是聲前一句？連云：聲前無句，聲後問將來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 林泉老人評唱投子青和尚頌古空谷集, case 74, Huanglian's phrase before sound. The exact headword-bearing speaker is an unnamed questioning monk: he asks Huanglian what a phrase before sound is, and Huanglian answers that before sound there is no phrase. All six rungs leave the monk unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 聲前一句，人人本具，放過一著，落在第二，若不放過，打出骨髓。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 密雲禪師語錄, hall address requested by layman Dong. Miyun Yuanwu is the exact speaker: he says everyone originally possesses the phrase before sound, and contrasts letting one move pass with striking out the marrow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 聲前一句。千聖不傳。未曾親覲。如隔大千。
